name: Inzing
kurzbeschreibung: Historic market town in the Oberinntal with a Baroque parish church and an impressive high altar – gateway to the Axamer Lizum.
beschreibung:
Overview

Inzing is situated at an elevation of 616 metres in the Tyrolean Inn Valley within the district of Innsbruck-Land, located approximately 20 kilometres west of Innsbruck between Zirl and Telfs. Home to around 4,000 residents, the municipality stretches from the sunny southern riverbanks of the Inn across fertile alluvial plains up into the alpine summits of the Stubai Alps beneath Mount Rangger Köpfl. Among its ecological treasures is the Gaisau nature reserve, one of the last preserved riparian floodplain forests bordering the Inn River, providing sanctuary for endangered bird and amphibian species. High in the mountains, the protected Hundstalsee lake stands out as an iconic natural monument. Inzing harmoniously unites vibrant village culture, high living quality within easy reach of the capital, and an array of outdoor activities spanning valley trails to high alpine peaks.

History

Archaeological finds confirm human presence on the local alluvial fan as early as the Bronze and Iron Ages, followed by Roman settlements. The village was first documented between 1022 and 1039 in records of the Prince-Bishopric of Freising under the Rhaeto-Romanic name Incingen. For centuries, Inzing flourished as an agricultural settlement sustained by farming, cattle breeding, and transport along the historical Inn Valley trade routes. The spiritual heart of the community is the Parish Church of St. Peter, originally constructed in late-Gothic style and comprehensively redesigned in 1779 by the celebrated Tyrolean church architect Franz de Paula Penz into a late-Baroque gem adorned with exquisite ceiling frescoes. The church achieved historic renown following a reported 1686 miracle in which tears were observed on an image of the Virgin Mary, sparking a popular pilgrimage.

Getting There

Inzing benefits from first-rate transport connectivity in central Tyrol. Motorists arrive smoothly via the Inntal Motorway A12 using exits at Zirl-West or Telfs-Ost, or along the toll-free federal highway B171. Rail access is equally convenient: Inzing railway station lies on the Arlberg railway line and is served by regular S-Bahn Tirol services (lines S4 and S5), connecting to Innsbruck Central Station in just 18 minutes. Long-distance cyclists can reach the village directly along the paved Inn River Cycle Path (Inntalradweg).

Tips

A truly extraordinary hiking destination is Lake Hundstalsee at an elevation of 2,289 metres. On its rugged shores, artists Robert Tribus and Heinz Triendl assembled roughly 350 tonnes of native dry stone between 1986 and 2006 to erect the majestic "Apollo Temple" (Apollontempel), an open-air art installation reflected in crystal-clear waters. For a gentler outing, hike up to the Inzinger Alm pasture at 1,641 metres, renowned for its hearty alpine refreshments and sweeping valley vistas. Nature enthusiasts will appreciate serene walks through the Gaisau wetlands along the Inn, while winter brings family skiing and tobogganing at the nearby Rangger Köpfl ski area in Oberperfuss.
